summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a Kea DHCP server on the private eth1 network (10.50.50.0/24, gateway 10.50.50.254, pool .100-.200), and configured node2/node3 (Alpine) eth1 interfaces to obtain addresses via DHCP instead of static assignment. Both nodes successfully leased addresses (node2=10.50.50.100, node3=10.50.50.101) from node1. Completed the mandatory sequential single-node restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected network topology: eth0 is the platform default DHCP/egress network on each node; eth1 is the shared private L2 network (initially down/unaddressed) meant for this task
Discovered current VyOS 2026.04-rolling Kea-based dhcp-server CLI syntax via /usr/libexec/vyos/tests/smoke/cli/test_service_dhcp-server.py since legacy isc-dhcp syntax failed on commit

Configured node1 eth1 static address 10.50.50.254/24 and a Kea DHCP server (shared-network LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, range 10.50.50.100-200, option default-router/name-server, lease 3600s); committed and saved to config.boot
Configured node2 and node3 /etc/network/interfaces adding 'auto eth1'/'iface eth1 inet dhcp', restarted networking, confirmed DHCP leases obtained from node1
Verified Kea lease database on node1 recorded both client leases with correct hostnames (node2, node3)
Captured baseline boot_id on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time, never concurrently), polling exec availability until each returned

Verified changed boot_id and post-restart health on each node: node1's DHCP server/config/lease-file persisted and resumed serving; node2 and node3 automatically re-acquired DHCP leases from node1 on boot via the persisted interfaces config

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DHCP server on private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: Kea DHCP server config committed and saved on node1 for shared-network LAN, subnet 10.50.50.0/24; config.boot and running kea-dhcp4.conf both show the applied config

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain eth1 address via DHCP from node1 instead of static assignment
evidence.summary: eth1 added as DHCP in /etc/network/interfaces on both nodes; dhcpcd logs show lease acquisition (node2: 10.50.50.100, node3: 10.50.50.101) and ip addr confirms dynamic scope addresses
node1 Kea lease CSV shows both client leases recorded with correct hostnames node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7668189d captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed to 36437d9e after reconnect; post-restart shows eth1 IP restored, kea-dhcp4 process running, lease file intact, config.boot persisted

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f9ad768d captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed to 20a60135 after reconnect; post-restart eth1 shows re-acquired DHCP lease 10.50.50.100 and persisted dhcp config in /etc/network/interfaces

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9194ed7d captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed to 310f1fc4 after reconnect; post-restart eth1 shows re-acquired DHCP lease 10.50.50.101 and persisted dhcp config in /etc/network/interfaces

evidence.requirement: post-restart cluster-wide DHCP service health (server side, after all three reboots)
evidence.summary: After node3's reboot, node1's kea-dhcp4 process still running and lease CSV shows fresh renewed leases for both node2 and node3, confirming the DHCP service survived all three node restarts and continues serving correctly
